transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martin (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood), Priya Kumar (AtlasFin CTO), Marcus Lee (ML Platform), Sara Thompson (Engineer)

AutoSummary: quick notes at top: POC scope to test JSON mode determinism, measure p50/p95 token latency and end-to-end time for tool-calling flow (invoke -> structured JSON response -> validation). POC to run on Dedicated capacity behind AtlasFin VPC.

[00:00:12] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this pretty technical — Diego's gonna walk through runtime numbers for json-mode and tool calls and then we'll talk POC.
[00:00:20] Priya Kumar: thanks, our main goal is to see deterministic JSON outputs for downstream processors and keep p95 below 200ms for single-turn API calls if possible, and of course data residency in our VPC.
[00:00:30] Diego Martin: got it. quick agenda: 1) what json-mode changes in decoding do, 2) how tool-calling affects latency and KV cache interaction, 3) batching/throughput tradeoffs, 4) quantization effects, 5) networking/VPC considerations.
[00:00:45] Marcus Lee: and also can you show the perf spreadsheet you mentioned earlier?
[00:00:52] Ava Chen: yes i'll drop the link in chat after — it's the benchmark sheet with per-model p50/p95, and a column for constrained-decoding overhead for structured outputs.

---
[00:02:10] Diego Martin: ok starting with json-mode: when we enable constrained decoding to force structured tokens (e.g., strict JSON grammar or limited token sets), we see a CPU-side token selection overhead. in hosted setups that translates to roughly +8-15% CPU time per token depending on model and tokenizer. for instance in our tests with a 13B encoder-decoder style model, generation time per token increased ~12% in JSON-mode vs unconstrained text.
[00:02:40] Sara Thompson: is that overhead constant or does it scale with sequence length?
[00:02:45] Diego Martin: it roughly scales with sequence length but there's a fixed per-step overhead for the constraint checks — the constraint automaton runs per decode step. so longer responses accumulate more overhead. short structured outputs (e.g., 20-80 tokens) see a higher relative overhead.

[00:03:20] Marcus Lee: what's the impact on KV-cache hits? we rely on heavy prefix caching.
[00:03:27] Diego Martin: good question — KV cache still functions the same; however, when you constrain decoding strictly to a grammar, you reduce stochasticity so the model often collapses into a narrower set of next-token predictions. that actually increases cache hit rate for repeated prompts/prefixes, because the attention footprints are more stable. in one of our Atlas-like workloads we saw small improvements in token reuse, lowering per-token compute by ~4% when combined with prefix caching. caveat: if your structured outputs include dynamic fields (timestamps, ids) that change each request, cache benefits are reduced.

[00:04:15] Priya Kumar: that aligns with our concern — we have dynamic IDs in payloads. can Redwood strip or normalize those prior to caching?
[00:04:23] Liam O'Neill: you can do prefix normalization or use a canonicalization step server-side; another option is keying the cache on a normalized prompt where dynamic fields are replaced with tokens like <ID>. we can help instrument that in the POC.

---
[00:05:10] Diego Martin: tool/function calling overhead: when the model emits a function call vs raw JSON, there's a small extra round trip in our runtime to parse the call, validate arguments, and optionally invoke external tools. end-to-end this adds ~10-30ms on top of generation for hosted infra; on Dedicated colocated with your network it's more like 5-15ms depending on the tool latency. the biggest delta is if you synchronously call external services — that can dominate.
[00:05:50] Marcus Lee: so for our use-case (call a pricing service after generating structured payload), we'd want asynchronous invocation? or local adapter?
[00:05:58] Diego Martin: yes we recommend either synchronous calls having very low-latency adapters within your VPC or an async pattern where the model returns the JSON and a job queue picks it up. for deterministic workflows we often do a sync internal adapter on Dedicated.

[00:06:30] Priya Kumar: numbers: you mentioned p95 goals — what did you observe for single-turn JSON-mode tool call with Dedicated vs Hosted?
[00:06:38] Diego Martin: example numbers from the bench (13B-ish, seq len ~120 tokens output): Hosted API (shared): p50 ~110ms, p95 ~260ms. Dedicated (reserved, colocated, optimized kernels): p50 ~70ms, p95 ~140ms. enabling JSON-mode moved the p95 up by ~10-20% in both cases. tool-calling overhead we saw +10-30ms when a synchronous adapter is added.
[00:07:10] Sara Thompson: that's borderline for our 200ms p95 target on Hosted but looks fine on Dedicated.

---
[00:08:05] Diego Martin: batching: batching improves throughput but increases head latency. with micro-batching (batch size 4-8) we saw throughput up by 3-4x but median latency increased by ~20-40ms per request due to queueing. continuous batching in our runtime tries to keep latency SLOs by adaptive batch cutoffs, but for very tight single-request SLOs we recommend Dedicated with smaller batch windows or per-request lanes.
[00:08:45] Marcus Lee: does json-mode affect batching efficiency?
[00:08:50] Diego Martin: it can. constrained decoding can make token generation more uniform which actually helps kernel-level packing, but the per-step automaton check adds CPU. overall batching still gives net win for throughput; the tradeoff is your p95 latency budget.

---
[00:09:30] Ava Chen: quick interjection — quantization, right? how does 4-bit quant affect structured output determinism?
[00:09:38] Diego Martin: quantization reduces model memory footprint; 4-bit methods with good quant-aware kernels can keep quality near FP16 for many tasks. but some models show slightly higher variance in low-probability tokens when quantized — that can matter for strict JSON schemas. empirically, 4-bit gave similar top-1 token accuracy for common tokens but increased rare-token noise, so you'd see a few syntactic hiccups occasionally on strict JSON. 8-bit tends to be safer if you require near-perfect grammar. for AtlasFin i'd recommend validating JSON with a post-parse and optionally running a constrained re-decoding step if the parse fails.

[00:10:25] Priya Kumar: if we do Dedicated with 4-bit, is there a way to force perfect grammar? re-decode until parse success?
[00:10:33] Diego Martin: yes. common pattern: constrained decoding + light post-check; if validation fails we can trigger a constrained re-ask (few-shot prompt) or use a deterministic sequenced decoder that enforces grammar. there's a latency cost for retries but it's predictable; in our tests a single re-decode added ~40-80ms depending on model size.

---
[00:11:15] Liam O'Neill: networking/VPC notes: for private deployment we support VPC peering and private links. Dedicated inside your VPC mitigates egress latency for tool adapters. make sure to share firewall rules and the CIDR blocks so we can pre-configure allowed endpoints. also if you require HSM/KMS integration for keys, we can germinate key wraps via your KMS.
[00:11:45] Marcus Lee: ok that's good. we'll want audit logs and per-request tracing for compliance.
[00:11:50] Ava Chen: Redwood Console provides token-level tracing and per-route dashboards; we can enable extended retention for your account as an add-on.

---
[00:12:30] Diego Martin: back to perf: I'll call out a few concrete bench cases we ran that are relevant to AtlasFin's ask — note these are synthetic but we can re-run on your exact prompts in the POC.
[00:12:40] Diego Martin: Test A: JSON-mode short payloads (~40 tokens). Model M13 (optimized kernels): Hosted p50=95ms p95=210ms; Dedicated p50=62ms p95=120ms. JSON-mode + strict grammar + validation step: Dedicated p95 ~170ms with a retry on ~3% of requests.
[00:13:05] Diego Martin: Test B: Tool-calling synchronous adapter (internal pricing lookup) — adapter latency 20ms: extra +20ms end-to-end in Dedicated, +30ms in Hosted due to additional network hop.
[00:13:22] Sara Thompson: do you have recommended batch window parameters?
[00:13:26] Diego Martin: our defaults: 5-20ms adaptive window for low-latency tiers; for throughput-optimized use 50-100ms windows. For AtlasFin p95 target, start with 5-10ms and Dedicated.

---
[00:14:10] Priya Kumar: about observability — can we get per-token timing and KV cache hit logs?
[00:14:16] Diego Martin: yes, we can surface token-level timing, KV cache hit/miss rates, and kernel selection logs. that will be part of the POC artifact bundle.

[00:14:40] Ava Chen: quick note on data controls: in Dedicated you can opt for customer-managed keys and local audit logs; for Private on-prem we can arrange air-gapped deployments but that extends lead time.

---
[00:15:05] Marcus Lee: what about concurrency? we'll have bursty traffic around end-of-day.
[00:15:10] Diego Martin: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies with burst capacity. importantly for JSON-mode and constrained decoding the CPU profile is slightly different, so autoscaler should consider both GPU and CPU headroom. we can provide recommended scaling rules after initial perf runs.

[00:15:45] Sara Thompson: any gotchas we should know before POC?
[00:15:48] Diego Martin: yes — canonicalization of dynamic fields (IDs, timestamps) for caching, planning for parser/retry logic for strict JSON, and ensuring low-latency adapters if you use synchronous tool-calls. also pick the right quantization tradeoff: 8-bit if grammar fidelity matters, 4-bit if memory constraints are tight and occasional re-decode is acceptable.

---
[00:16:30] Ava Chen: we'll summarize next steps: I'll send the benchmark sheet, Diego will run the Atlas sample tests, and we'll schedule the POC kickoff.
[00:16:40] Priya Kumar: sounds good. can you include a sample POC timeline and acceptance criteria (latency thresholds, error rates for parse failures)?
[00:16:48] Ava Chen: yes — will include in runbook. proposed acceptance: p95 under 160ms on Dedicated for typical short JSON payloads with parse failure <1% after retry logic; tooling adapter latency <20ms for sync calls.

---

[00:51:05] Ava Chen: recap and action items (see top). i will also share SOC2 & VPC docs in the next message.
